# Dreikönigsaktion – Hilfswerk der Katholischen Jungschar (DKA Austria)

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-30 · status **partial** · Search/document budget spent (~9 searches, 2 PDF fetches plus several page reads). No India-specific financial figures (spend amounts, grant sizes with currency/unit) were located on the readable pages checked; DKA's own annual financial reports were not found in a readable form within budget. A page titled 'DKA-Kfb – Bosco Institute' (boscoinstitute.org/dka-kfb) that might confirm a third India partner is HELD (robots.txt unreadable) and could not be quoted.

DKA Austria (Dreikönigsaktion – Hilfswerk der Katholischen Jungschar) is the development-cooperation agency of Austria's Catholic Children's Movement (Jungschar), funded by the annual Carol Singers' Campaign and supporting ~500 projects/year in Africa, Asia/Oceania (incl. India, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines) and Latin America; it does not implement projects itself but funds partner NGOs via a standing application process (minimum standards, preference to existing partners, decision by an Inter-Diocesan Committee meeting three times a year, typical project duration ~3 years). kfb Austria (Katholische Frauenbewegung Österreichs, kfbö) is a separate but closely linked organisation - Austria's largest Catholic women's movement, part of Katholische Aktion Österreich - whose Aktion Familienfasttag (Family Fast Day) campaign since 1958 funds ~70 projects for women's organisations in the Global South, with project selection done 'in cooperation with' DKA. Neither DKA nor kfb are Section 135-bound Indian CSR entities; no India-specific spend figures with currency/unit were found on the pages read. kfb's current featured India partner is SEEDS (Socio Economic and Education Development Society), working with indigenous (Adivasi) women across roughly 131-300 villages/communities in Jharkhand; Thoughtshop Foundation (TSF) and a project called CASS are also named on kfb's India page, without amounts. No grant amounts, multi-year India spend trend, or a currently open dated RFP/deadline were found; the funding process is best described as a standing, largely invitation/relationship-preferred application channel rather than a dated call.

Website: https://www.dka.at

## What it set out to find

- identity: confirm legal names and relationship of DKA Austria and kfb Austria
- csr_year/csr_spend: latest annual India-directed spend and 2-3 prior years, FY-labelled
- footprint vs stated_geography: states/districts where India projects actually ran vs stated priority countries
- partner: named Indian partner NGOs, project titles, amounts where disclosed
- how to apply: grant size, eligibility, process, open/rolling/invitation-only, deadlines, contact
- evidence: annual report / website / partner pages with quotes and URLs

## Programmes

  > Der Familienfasttag versteht sich als langfristige entwicklungspolitische Initiative.
